:::{#def-block-matrix}
#### Block matrix

Split the rows of an $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{X}$ into the first $k$ and the last $m - k$,
and its columns into the first $l$ and the last $n - l$,
with $1 \le k < m$ and $1 \le l < n$.
This cuts $\matr{X}$ into four smaller matrices, its **blocks**:

$$
\matr{X} = \begin{bmatrix} \matr{A} & \matr{B} \\ \matr{C} & \matr{D} \end{bmatrix},
$$

where $\matr{A}$ ($k \times l$) holds the entries $x_{ij}$ with $i \le k$ and $j \le l$,
$\matr{B}$ ($k \times (n - l)$) those with $i \le k$ and $j > l$,
$\matr{C}$ ($(m - k) \times l$) those with $i > k$ and $j \le l$,
and $\matr{D}$ ($(m - k) \times (n - l)$) those with $i > k$ and $j > l$,
each in its original order.
A matrix written this way is a **block matrix**.
When $\matr{X}$ is $n \times n$ and $1 \le k \le n$,
the $k \times k$ matrix of the entries $x_{ij}$ with $i, j \le k$
is the **leading** (or **top-left**) $k \times k$ **block** of $\matr{X}$;
for $k < n$ it is the block $\matr{A}$ above with $l = k$,
and for $k = n$ it is $\matr{X}$ itself.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-block-matrix}
#### Cutting a $3 \times 3$ matrix into blocks

With

$$
\begin{aligned}
k &= l \\
&= 1,
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\matr{X} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 6 \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} \matr{A} & \matr{B} \\ \matr{C} & \matr{D} \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\matr{C} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\matr{D} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ 3 & 6 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

For instance, entry $(1, 2)$ of $\matr{D}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{1 + 1, 2 + 1} &= x_{23} \\
&= 3.
\end{aligned}
$$

With

$$
\begin{aligned}
k &= l \\
&= 2
\end{aligned}
$$

instead, the leading $2 \times 2$ block is
$\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$.

:::
